newsitem.title: POLAND: SWISS-BRITISH CONSORTIUM OFFERS POLAND FIGHTERS.
newsitem.headline: SWISS-BRITISH CONSORTIUM OFFERS POLAND FIGHTERS.

text.p: A consortium of Sweden's Saab and British Aerospace on Thursday said its offer to sell Poland fighter jets was 40-percent cheaper than those by companies from the United States.

"According to our initial calculations the offer by Saab and British Aerospace is, under a package we are preparing, 40- percent cheaper than the American offers," Alan Garwood, Aerospace's director for North America and Europe, told Reuters.

The consortium presented its state-of-the-art JAS 39 Gripen jet during a military arms fair in the Baltic port of Gdynia to rival the F-16 and F-18 fighters offered by U.S. Lockheed Martin and McDonnell Douglas respectively.
The three companies and French Dassault , with its Mirage 2000, plan to bid in a tender likely to be launched next year to gradually replace about 100 of Poland's outmoded fighters.

Garwood said his company was preparing for the government and Polish arms manufacturers a broad offer of cooperation containing exports guarantees by the British and Swiss governments for the fighter sale.
Lockheed and McDonnel have already unveiled their cooperation offers, which include 100-percent offset contracts for Poland's arms industry if the deal is clinched.
The U.S. companies have made similar offers to the Czech Republic and Hungary, which also need new fighters to upgrade their armed forces to NATO standards.
Lockheed has said the contract with Poland would be worth between $100 million and $1.5 billion.
